# Model card: the two demo models

Format inspired by Mitchell et al., *Model Cards for Model Reporting* (2019). This card describes the models of
the two demos; the other methods of the project are compared in the [README](README.md).

| | Online demo | Local demo |
|---|---|---|
| Where | [Hugging Face Space](https://huggingface.co/spaces/leliondu972/metastasis-across-hospitals), in the visitor's browser ([web/](web/)) | `python app/app.py` ([app/](app/)) |
| Model | {{web_method}} | Frozen Phikon ViT-B/16 + linear head |
| Why this model | Best CNN on the validation hospital, small enough for a web page | Best method on the validation hospital |
| Accuracy on the test hospital | {{web_acc_test}}% | {{app_acc_test}}% |

## Model details

**Online demo: {{web_method}}**

- **Architecture:** DenseNet-121 trained from scratch (the WILDS baseline), with random changes of the hematoxylin
  and eosin amounts at training time only (HED stain augmentation).
- **Training:** WILDS ERM protocol (SGD, 10 epochs) on the training hospitals of Camelyon17-WILDS, epoch chosen on
  the validation hospital. Seed {{web_seed}}, chosen on the validation hospital (see Selection).
- **Post-processing:** temperature {{web_temperature}}, fitted on the validation hospital; patches whose score is
  not confident enough are referred to a pathologist (cutoff chosen on the validation hospital).
- **Explanation:** Grad-CAM on the last block (3 x 3 grid). Since the network ends with a ReLU, global average
  pooling and a linear layer, Grad-CAM equals CAM (Zhou et al., 2016): the exported model computes the map
  directly, without gradients.
- **Format:** ONNX, run by ONNX Runtime Web in the visitor's browser; no image is sent anywhere.
- **License:** MIT (code and weights).

**Local demo: frozen Phikon + linear head**

- **Architecture:** Phikon ViT-B/16 (Owkin, pretrained on histology), frozen, pinned revision; its [CLS] token
  is standardized with the mean and standard deviation of the training patches, then a linear layer gives a
  tumor score.
- **Training:** the linear layer only, with the same protocol on the same hospitals. Seed {{app_seed}}, chosen on
  the validation hospital (see Selection).
- **Post-processing:** temperature {{app_temperature}}, fitted on the validation hospital; referral as above.
- **Explanation:** Grad-CAM at the input of the last transformer block (14 x 14 grid).
- **Licenses:** code MIT; Phikon weights under the Owkin non-commercial license, so this model is for
  non-commercial research and education only.

## Intended use

- Demonstrating, for research and teaching, how a metastasis detector behaves on a hospital it was not
  trained on: score, heat map, referral of uncertain patches.
- **Not a medical device. Not for diagnosis or any clinical decision.**

## Out of scope

Whole-slide or patient-level diagnosis; other organs, stains or magnifications than 96 x 96 H&E lymph-node
patches of Camelyon17-WILDS (other images are cropped and resized, and the output is unreliable); commercial use
of the local demo.

## Data

- **Training:** Camelyon17-WILDS train split, hospitals 0, 3 and 4 ({{n_train}} patches).
- **Selection:** validation hospital (hospital 1, {{n_val}} patches, {{n_patients_val}} patients), never seen
  in training.
- **Test:** hospital 2 ({{n_test}} patches, {{n_patients_test}} patients), never seen in training and never
  used to choose anything.
- No demographic information is available, so performance across patient groups could not be assessed.

## Selection

Both models were chosen on the validation hospital, never on the test hospital. The local demo uses the best
method on that hospital (mean of {{n_seeds}} seeds); the online demo, which must run in a browser, the best CNN.
For each, the seed is the one with the highest validation accuracy:

- **Online demo:** {{web_val_by_seed}}.
- **Local demo:** {{app_val_by_seed}}.

The Phikon seeds are equivalent, and the rule just picks one. The CNN seeds are not: the best one on the
validation hospital is below its method's mean on the test hospital ({{web_acc_test}}% against
{{web_method_acc_test}}%). One validation hospital is a weak guide, for seeds as for methods.

## Results of each model

| Patches | Online demo: accuracy | AUC | Local demo: accuracy | AUC |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Training hospitals (id_val, held-out patches of the training slides) | {{web_acc_id_val}}% | {{web_auc_id_val}} | {{app_acc_id_val}}% | {{app_auc_id_val}} |
| Validation hospital (used for selection) | {{web_acc_val}}% | {{web_auc_val}} | {{app_acc_val}}% | {{app_auc_val}} |
| Test hospital (unseen, never used to choose) | **{{web_acc_test}}%** | {{web_auc_test}} | **{{app_acc_test}}%** | {{app_auc_test}} |

- Over {{n_seeds}} seeds, the two methods reach {{web_method_acc_test}}% and {{acc_test_probe_phikon}}% on the
  test hospital, with 95% intervals {{web_method_ci_test}} and {{ci_test_probe_phikon}} when its
  {{n_patients_test}} patients are redrawn: the uncertainty is large.
- **Referral:** the cutoffs, set on the validation hospital, make the models answer {{web_answered_val}}% (online)
  and {{app_answered_val}}% (local) of its patches. On the test hospital, the online model answers
  {{web_answered_test}}% of patches and its error goes from {{web_error_all_test}}% to
  {{web_error_answered_test}}%; the local model answers {{app_answered_test}}%, and its error goes from
  {{app_error_all_test}}% to {{app_error_answered_test}}%.
- **Calibration:** expected calibration error on the test hospital, before and after the temperature:
  {{web_ece_test_before}} → {{web_ece_test_after}} online, {{app_ece_test_before}} → {{app_ece_test_after}}
  locally. The score is calibrated for one hospital only; elsewhere it is a ranking, not an exact probability.

## Checks

- **Online:** the exported model reproduces the saved predictions of its run (largest probability gap
  {{web_max_gap}}, {{web_same_decisions}};
  [results/tables/web_demo_checks.json](results/tables/web_demo_checks.json), rerun by
  `python -m src.check_web_demo`). A test checks that its heat map, computed without gradients, equals the
  Grad-CAM of the analyses ([tests/test_web_demo.py](tests/test_web_demo.py)).
- **Local:** the demo reproduces the saved predictions of its run (largest probability gap {{app_max_gap}},
  {{app_same_decisions}}; [results/tables/app_checks.json](results/tables/app_checks.json)). Its heat map
  depends on the learned weights: with the last block randomized, its rank correlation with the original map
  falls to {{app_randomization}}.

## Caveats

- The online model is the less accurate of the two on the test hospital ({{web_acc_test}}% against
  {{app_acc_test}}%): it was chosen because it runs in a browser, and its page says so.
- Two unseen hospitals only; nothing guarantees the results on a third one.
- Labels come from hand-drawn contours and describe the central 32 x 32 region of each patch; some patches
  that every method gets wrong are candidates for ambiguous labels.
- A heat map shows which regions push the score towards tumor, not the model's reasoning.
